$comment: Plain-language glossary for the pre-lab training decks. Each entry is one product or AI term, defined once in words a newcomer understands (about grade 8). `match` lists the surface forms a deck scans for so the term is explained the first time it appears; `plain` is the one-line definition shown inline, on the Key terms slide, and in the speaker notes. `expansion` is the full wording for an acronym. Every definition follows Microsoft Learn; nothing here is invented product behavior. Part files named terms-*.json in this folder add more terms; an id may be defined only once across all of them.

agent.plain: an AI assistant that follows your instructions, reads your content, and uses tools to get work done

ai-model.plain: the AI system that reads a request and writes a response

generative-ai.plain: AI that writes new text or other content in reply to a request

prompt.plain: the text you give an AI model to tell it what you want

instructions.plain: plain-language rules that tell an agent its job, its tone, and its limits

knowledge.plain: content an agent can read to answer questions, such as sites, files, and business data

grounding.plain: basing an answer on specific content instead of the model's general memory

citation.plain: a note that shows which source an answer came from

tool.plain: an action an agent can take, such as looking up a record or sending a message

connector.plain: a ready-made link to another service, so an agent can read or change its data

topic.plain: a reusable conversation path for one subject, such as resetting a password

orchestration.plain: how an agent decides what to do next with each request

generative-orchestration.plain: orchestration where the AI model picks the topics, tools, and knowledge to use, based on their descriptions

classic-orchestration.plain: orchestration that picks a topic by matching a person's words to its trigger phrases

trigger.plain: an event or phrase that starts a topic or an agent's work

channel.plain: a place where people talk to an agent, such as Microsoft Teams or a website

publish.plain: make the latest saved version of an agent available to people

harness.plain: the kind of agent engine you build on; Copilot Studio offers more than one

environment.plain: a space in Power Platform that holds your agents, data, and settings

solution.plain: a package that carries apps and agents from one environment to another

dataverse.plain: the Power Platform data service that stores business records in tables

sharepoint.plain: Microsoft's service for team sites, document libraries, and lists

entra-id.plain: Microsoft's sign-in service that proves who a person is

permissions.plain: rules that decide who can see or change something

data-policy.plain: a data loss prevention (DLP) rule that limits which services can share data

mcp.plain: the Model Context Protocol, an open standard that lets an agent find and use tools from a server

agent-flow.plain: a set of automated steps that runs when an agent or an event starts it

power-fx.plain: the low-code formula language used across Power Platform

adaptive-card.plain: a small card of text, images, and buttons that shows up inside a chat

variable.plain: a named value an agent remembers during a conversation

entity.plain: a kind of detail an agent can pick out of a message, such as a date or a city

evaluation.plain: a test run that scores how well an agent answers a set of questions

copilot-credits.plain: the units Copilot Studio uses to measure how much an agent is used

m365-copilot.plain: Microsoft's AI assistant built into Microsoft 365 apps such as Word and Teams

declarative-agent.plain: an agent for Microsoft 365 Copilot that you define with instructions, knowledge, and actions

sub-agent.plain: another agent your agent hands part of a job to

memory.plain: details an agent keeps from earlier conversations so it can help with context

skill.plain: a saved, reusable ability an agent can call on

api.plain: a way for one program to ask another program for data or actions

foundry.plain: Microsoft's platform for building AI apps and agents with models

model-deployment.plain: a copy of an AI model set up so apps can call it

quota.plain: the most of a service you are allowed to use

ai-builder.plain: a Power Platform feature for building and using AI models and prompts in apps and flows

alm.plain: application lifecycle management: moving changes from building to testing to live use

rbac.plain: giving people only the roles they need, and nothing more

sensitivity-label.plain: a tag on a file that sets how carefully it must be handled
